title: High-Throughput Identification of Resistance to Pseudomonas syringae pv. Tomato in Tomato using Seedling Flood Assay
protocol: Wipe down biosafety cabinet with 70% ethanol.
Close sash and turn on ultraviolet light for 15 min.
Turn off ultraviolet light after 15 min.
Lift sash and turn on blower for 15 min.
Wipe items to be used in the biosafety cabinet with 70% ethanol before placing them inside.
Clean gloves or bare hands with 70% ethanol before working in the biosafety cabinet.
Work in the center of the biosafety cabinet, away from the blower.
Use unopened bottles of autoclaved sterile 10 mM MgCl2 and ultrapure H2O for experiments.
Open bottles only inside the sterilized biosafety cabinet, not on the benchtop.
Use dedicated glass pipettes and pipette tips for work in the sterilized biosafety cabinet.
Ensure that pipettes and tips are opened only inside the biosafety cabinet, never on the benchtop.
Autoclave all waste except bleach waste after use of the biosafety cabinet.
Wipe down surface with 70% ethanol after using the biosafety cabinet.
Weigh out and dissolve 0.5x MS basal salts in ultrapure H2O.
Weigh out 0.8% bacto agar and add to dissolved 0.5x MS.
Autoclave prepared media.
Allow media to cool in a 50 °C water bath for 1 h prior to pouring or pipetting.
Mark polystyrene disposable sterile 100 x 25 mm plates to a fill level of 40 mL.
Pour media into 100 x 25 mm sterile plates in a sterilized biosafety cabinet.
Place tomato seeds in a 2.2 mL microcentrifuge tube and add 2.0 mL of 50% bleach solution.
Rock the tube on a rocker for 25 min.
Remove the bleach solution with a pipette in the sterile biosafety cabinet.
Add 2 mL of sterile ultrapure H2O to wash the seeds.
Invert the tube 5x.
Repeat steps to wash the seeds 4 more times.
Pour the seeds into an empty sterile Petri dish after the final wash.
Flame forceps in ethanol and allow to cool prior to transferring seeds.
Transfer and evenly space seeds on 100 x 25 mm plates containing 0.5x MS + 0.8% agar media using cooled, sterilized forceps.
Transfer 5–7 seeds in a line across the middle of one plate.
Seal the edges of the plates with surgical tape (1.25 cm x 9.1 m).
Stratify the sterilized seeds at 4 °C in the dark for at least 3 days to synchronize germination.
Stack the plates flat and face up so that the seeds do not shift on the plate.
Vertically orient the plates so that the roots will grow down along the surface of the plate when transferring to the growth chamber.
Set the growth chamber to 22 °C.
Provide 16 hours of light at a light intensity of ~200–220 µE m\(^{-2}\) s\(^{-1}\).
Provide 8 hours of darkness.
Grow seedlings for 10 days in the growth chamber.
Fill a beaker with 500 mL of ultrapure H2O and stir on a stir plate.
Dissolve 20 g of bacto peptone, 1.5 g of anhydrous K2HPO4, and 12.5 mL of glycerol in the beaker with ultrapure H2O.
Pour the dissolved mixture into a 1 L graduated cylinder and bring up to a final volume of 1 L with ultrapure H2O.
Pour the broth back into the beaker and stir until mixed.
Weigh out 7.5 g of bacto agar into two 500 mL glass bottles.
Add 500 mL of KB broth from step 4.4 into each bottle.
Autoclave for 20 minutes.
Remove the bottles from the autoclave and swirl gently to distribute the agar.
Transfer the bottles to a 50 °C water bath for 1 h.
Transfer the bottle to the biosafety cabinet after 1 h.
Add 1,600 µL of sterile 1 M MgSO4 and appropriate antibiotics to the media.
Swirl the media gently to mix thoroughly.
Pour the media to cover the bottom of the plates.
Allow at least 1 h for the plates to solidify before storing them upside down at 4 °C.
Patch bacteria from a glycerol stock onto KB agar with appropriate antibiotics.
Allow the bacteria to recover for 2 days at 28 °C.
Streak fresh bacteria from the glycerol stock onto appropriate selective KB agar using a flat, sterile toothpick.
Incubate the KB plate at 28 °C for 48 h prior to using bacteria in the flood experiment.
Aseptically resuspend the bacteria in sterile 10 mM MgCl2 to an optical density at 600 nm (OD600) of 0.1, or approximately 5 x 10^7 CFU/mL.
Perform serial dilutions using sterile 10 mM MgCl2 solution.
Use a spectrophotometer to make inoculum with a starting concentration of OD600 = 0.1 for Pst19.
Make a 1/10 dilution from the initial resuspension at OD600 = 0.1 to obtain a serial dilution at a concentration of OD600 = 0.01 for Pst19.
Make a 3/4 dilution of the serial dilution at OD600 = 0.01 to obtain a final OD600 = 0.0075 for Pst19.
Make a 1/10 dilution of non-ionic organosilicone surfactant copolymer C13H34O4Si3 in 10 mM MgCl2 and vortex for 15 s.
Add the 1/10 stock of surfactant to the last serial dilution (OD600 = 0.0075) to a final concentration of 0.015% and swirl well to mix.
Aseptically resuspend bacteria in sterile 10 mM MgCl2 to an optical density at 600 nm (OD600) of 0.1 for PstDC3000, approximately 5 x 10^7 CFU/mL.
Perform serial dilutions using sterile 10 mM MgCl2 solution in the biosafety cabinet.
Use a spectrophotometer to make inoculum with a starting concentration of OD600 = 0.1 for PstDC3000.
Dilute PstDC3000 from an initial OD600 = 0.1 to obtain a concentration of OD600 = 0.01.
Make a further dilution of the previous serial dilution (OD600 = 0.01) to achieve a final OD600 = 0.005.
Prepare a 1/10 dilution of surfactant in 10 mM MgCl2 and vortex for 15 seconds.
Add the 1/10 stock of surfactant to the last serial dilution (OD600 = 0.005) to a final concentration of 0.015% and mix well.
Take plates with 10-day-old seedlings out of the growth chamber and prepare them for flooding in the biosafety cabinet.
Remove surgical tape from two plates.
Measure 6 mL of inoculum (OD600 = 0.005) and transfer to each plate containing 10-day-old seedlings.
Gently push down the seedlings into the inoculum with a sterile pipette tip.
Tilt the front of the plate down to accumulate inoculum, mainly submerging cotyledons and leaves.
Swish side to side 5–7 times and then tip plates back to cover roots and whole plate.
Repeat tilting process to submerge cotyledons and leaves for a total of 3 minutes.
Pour off inoculum from the plates and set them down on a flat surface.
Pour off any residual inoculum a second time.
Rewrap the plates with surgical tape.
Repeat steps 8.2–8.8 for any remaining plates.
Re-incubate the plates in the growth chamber after all plates have been flooded.
Phenotype after 7–10 days for PstDC3000 or 10–14 days for Pst19.
Collect leaf tissue after 4 days if carrying out bacterial growth assays.
Perform phenotypic analysis and bacterial growth assays on separate sets of plants if necessary.
Remove the plates with tomato seedlings from the growth chamber four days post-flooding.
Number individual seedlings where they attach to the plate.
Label sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes with individual seedling numbers.
Drop one 3 mm sterile borosilicate bead into each tube for use with a bead beater.
Pipette 200 µL of 10 mM MgCl2 into each tube and close tubes.
Prepare 70% ethanol and pour 100 mL into a clean beaker.
Pour 100 mL of sterile ultrapure H2O into a separate, clean beaker.
Clean stainless steel straight fine-point forceps with serrated tips with ethanol.
Open the plate slightly to allow aseptic removal of one cotyledon with the clean forceps.
Pinch the petiole at the base of the cotyledon to remove it.
Drop the cotyledon into a beaker with 70% ethanol for surface sterilization for 10 seconds.
Rinse the cotyledon in ultrapure water for 10 seconds.
Place the cotyledon on a paper towel and blot dry with delicate science wipes.
Individually weigh each surface-sterilized cotyledon and record its weight.
Place the cotyledon in a previously prepared 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube labeled with the corresponding genotype and individual number.
Reseal the plates with sterile tape.
Re-incubate the seedlings in the growth chamber.
Homogenize the tissue using a bead beater in 10 mM MgCl2 for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add 800 µL of 10 mM MgCl2 to each tube containing macerated tissue and invert several times to mix thoroughly.
Prepare serial dilutions for each sample in 10 mM MgCl2 using a multichannel pipette.
Pipette 5 μL from each dilution series using a multichannel pipette onto a KB agar plate with cycloheximide.
Let the plates dry completely.
Incubate the plate upside down at 28 °C for 36 h.
Visualize the colonies on the plates using a dissecting microscope to determine if the colonies are large enough to count.
If the colonies are not large enough, re-incubate the plates and recheck the size of the colonies every few hours.
Count colonies under a dissecting microscope before they merge.
Count colonies from dilution series plates with fewer than 100 colonies.
Normalize colony counts to 0.1 g of tissue for seedlings.
Convert normalized colony counts to log bacterial growth.
Calculate the adjusted number of colonies as (C2 x 0.1 g) / B2.
Calculate the total number of colonies as (D2 x E2 x F2).
Average the total number of colonies across samples.
Calculate the average log growth as log(H2).
Normalize colony counts to 0.1 g of tissue based on the average mass of one MoneyMaker-PtoS cotyledon.
Remove the plates from the growth chamber and phenotype individual seedlings for death or survival after 7–14 days.
Phenotype plants infected with PstDC3000 earlier, at 7–10 days after flood inoculation.
Phenotype plants infected with Pst19 at 10–14 days after flood inoculation.
Determine a scoring system based on the range of resistance phenotypes observed.
Record binary phenotypes for cultivars, isogenic lines, and wild accessions with consistent, strong to intermediate resistance phenotypes.
Monitor seedlings for new growth from the apical meristem within the phenotyping time frame.
Count seedlings displaying new green vegetative growth as survivors.
Record seedlings with brown apical meristems and no new growth as deaths.
Record phenotypes on a disease spectrum for populations, such as F2 mapping populations, with varying resistance levels.
Monitor seedlings carefully for disease symptoms and death to identify the appropriate timing for phenotyping.
